{{dablink|"Thompson subgroup" can also mean an analogue of the Weyl group used in the [[classical involution theorem]]}}
In [[Group theory#Finite group theory|finite group theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]], the '''Thompson subgroup''' <math>J(P)</math> of a [[finite group|finite]] [[p-group|''p''-group]] ''P'' refers to one of several [[characteristic subgroup]]s of ''P''. {{harvs|txt|last=Thompson|first=John G.|authorlink=John G. Thompson|year=1964}} originally defined <math>J(P)</math> to be the subgroup generated by the [[abelian group|abelian]] [[subgroup]]s of ''P'' of maximal [[Rank of a group|rank]]. More often the Thompson subgroup   <math>J(P)</math>  is defined to be the subgroup generated by the abelian subgroups of ''P'' of maximal [[order (group theory)|order]] or the subgroup generated by the [[elementary abelian group|elementary abelian]] subgroups of ''P'' of maximal rank. In general these three subgroups can be different, though they are all called the Thompson subgroup and denoted by <math>J(P)</math>.
